title: The new rule decides which fence lines pair up by position alone: with an odd number of fence lines it pairs the first,
acceptanceReason: latent, no plan affected today; the CommonMark fence rule plus a diagnostic line is the next slice

specimenFacts.fact: I built the changed engine from the implementer worktree (go build -o $TMPDIR/ms ./cmd/metasystem) and ran it against a plan file containing, in order: a line of three backticks followed by "text"; "- Next step: REAL work to do"; another three-backtick line followed by "text"; "- Next step: FAKE example"; a bare three-backtick line. The engine printed "OPEN-WORK plans/strayfirst.md: FAKE example" and never printed "REAL work to do". Two things make this worse than a taste question. First, in real Markdown a fence line carrying an info string cannot close a fence, so both fields sit inside one code block and neither should be reported; the engine reports one of them. Second, the behaviour before this whole chain reported the FIRST matching field, which for this file is the real one, so on this shape the new rule is a step backwards, not forwards. A rule that satisfies every test now in the tree AND this case exists and is no larger than the one written: scan once, let a fence open on any three-backtick line, let it close only on a bare three-backtick line, and if the end of the file arrives with a fence still open, treat that unmatched opener as ordinary text and read the fields after it. On the round-two trap plan that rule excludes the fake field and reports the real one; on this plan it reports nothing; on the existing unclosed-fence test it still finds the real field. I note for the orchestrator that the review brief's threat model asks about "the odd-count rule treating the FIRST unmatched fence as text instead of the LAST", which is a neighbouring worry rather than this one; whether that puts this finding inside or outside the declared scope is the orchestrator's call, not mine.

title: A reachable seat with a stalled progress card or dead card writer can receive the green “All good on this computer”
acceptanceReason: Accepted by m1e in Wido word: the accepted design puts stuck seats in Needs you with Stop in step 2; step 1 is read-only plus Land now. Fix in step 2.

specimenFacts.fact: metasystem/internal/board/board.go:140-153 and :190-200 classify a stalled card as unknown; :204-220 likewise classify a dead writer. The board payload carries that classification, but metasystem/internal/ui/web/_app/src/fleet/panel.ts:252-264 collects needs only from fleet silence, local health, lane, and questions. Its Doing rule drops unknown cards at :543-569, while its verdict returns All good when that list is empty at :169-183. A machine can remain reachable while its separate card writer stalls, so the fleet silence rule at metasystem/internal/ui/fleet/fleet.go:357-368 does not cover it.

acceptanceReason: Accepted by m1e in Wido word (land fast, fix non-breaking forward): improbable, needs two review rooms changing one record at the moment of a verdict; fix forward as a follow-up on this goal

specimenFacts.fact: metasystem/internal/ui/act/review.go:57-63 reads the record and compares its revision, then lines 64-81 perform further work and pass the captured bytes to goal.Review without another record check. metasystem/internal/goal/review.go:334-339 publishes those captured bytes.
